messages:
jess: Quick sync — I'm about to land TF that adds a capacity reservation + spot fallback for the GPU nodepools in prod. Need a quick sanity check on labels/taints and secret wiring before I apply.

jess: TL;DR of changes: add capacity reservation for p4d pool, introduce a spot pool (mixed h100/g5) with lower priority, taint reserved pool with `gpu=reserved:NoSchedule`, spot pool has toleration + cheaper lifecycle. Also wiring an SSM param for the AMI and a KMS-encrypted user_data secret for node bootstrap.

kyle: Sounds sensible. Two quick q's: 1) How do we prevent latency-sensitive pods from landing on spot? 2) How will the capacity reservation interact with autoscaler?

jess: For (1) we rely on node labels and pod affinity: pods that require stable throughput will have `nodeSelector: redwood.com/gpu_class: reserved` (or an annotation we map in the webhook). For (2) capacity reservation will be carved out of the reservation pool; autoscaler will scale the on-demand pool only when reservation is full. The spot pool is autoscaled independently and will never preempt the reservations.

chen: Can you paste the TF snippet + example pod toleration/selector? I want to validate nothing breaks our admission controller assumptions.

jess: Sure — snippet below. Note: this is pseudo-TF trimmed for the thread.

```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "p4d_reserve" {
  instance_type           = "p4d.24xlarge"
  availability_zone       = var.prod_az
  instance_count          = 2
  tags = {
    Name = "redwood-gpu-p4d-reserve"
  }
}

resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_reserved_lt" {
  name_prefix = "gpu-reserved-"
  image_id    = data.aws_ami.gpu.id
  user_data   = base64encode(data.aws_ssm_parameter.gpu_bootstrap.value)
  iam_instance_profile = aws_iam_instance_profile.gpu_profile.name
  // other networking / iam bits
}

module "eks_node_group_reserved" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/eks-nodepool-module"
  name   = "gpu-reserved"
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge"]
  desired_size   = 2
  launch_template = aws_launch_template.gpu_reserved_lt.id
  tags = { "redwood.com/gpu_class" = "reserved" }
}

module "eks_node_group_spot" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/eks-nodepool-module"
  name   = "gpu-spot"
  instance_types = ["h100","g5.12xlarge"]
  spot        = true
  desired_size = 0
  max_size     = 10
  tags = { "redwood.com/gpu_class" = "spot" }
}
```

jess: k8s pod snippet we plan to use for latency-sensitive services:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-infer
  annotations:
    redwood.com/gpu_class: reserved
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "reserved"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    redwood.com/gpu_class: reserved
  containers:
  - name: model
    image: ghcr.io/redwood/infer:stable
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

maria: small nit — prefer label `redwood.com/gpu_class` rather than `node.k8s.redwood/gpu-class` so it's consistent with the console filters. Also double-check the taint key format to avoid collisions.

jess: good catch, i'll standardize to `redwood.com/gpu_class`.

chen: on secret wiring — where is the SSM param created? I want to ensure we don't accidentally reference a dev-only param in prod.

jess: we create `aws_ssm_parameter.prod/gpu_bootstrap` in the infra-account TF module (same repo). The value is KMS encrypted userdata that pulls kubelet certs and docker credentials. I'll add a preflight check to validate the param exists in prod and point the launch_template to it.

infra-bot: terraform plan for branch `gpu/reserve-spot-fallback` is available: https://infra.internal/plan/5829 — 5 resources to add, 1 to change.

kyle: Quick runtime question — draining: how do we handle spot evictions? Do we want a graceful drain window or immediate fallback to reserved?

jess: plan: spot eviction handler (k8s DaemonSet) will cordon + evict non-critical pods quickly, and controller will retry to schedule critical pods onto reserved pool using a failover webhook that rewrites nodeSelector if necessary. We'll also set a 2m preemption buffer in the eviction-handler to allow a short teardown.

maria: sounds fine. Can you also add an alert mapping for spot eviction spikes in the gpu namespace? want alerting when >3 spot evictions/min for 5m.

jess: will add an alert. Also opening PR #4523 with the TF and chart changes. If no objections by EOD PST I'll merge and apply during our low-traffic window tomorrow 06:00 UTC.

kyle: LGTM from me, ty.

chen: lgtm pending the prod-ssm preflight.

jess: thanks all — will add preflight and update the PR. If anything else, ping me or leave comments on the PR. :rocket:
